summary: Black Rock Harbor (Fayerweather Island) Light, Bridgeport, Connecticut: lit from 1808-1809, a stone tower since 1823, discontinued 1933, now a city park.

lens.note: The archive lists a fifth-order Fresnel as the current optic; no source gives its present location.

structures.note: Forty feet tall; destroyed in the hurricane of 3 September 1821 (LighthouseFriends).

structures.type: octagonal stone tower, coursed sandstone ashlar with rubble mortar
structures.note: Cost $2,300 to build (LighthouseFriends). Lighting equipment added later; not an official aid to navigation.
New keeper's dwelling built in 1879 (LighthouseFriends); the archive gives 1880. Burned to the ground in 1977.

staffing.note: LighthouseFriends gives 3 March 1933 for discontinuance; the archive gives 1932.

access.note: Grounds reached from the parking area at the end of Barnum Boulevard at Seaside Park; a rough breakwater leads to the lighthouse; the tower is not open to the public.

visit.note: The tower itself is not open to the public (D'Entremont).

facts.agency: City of Bridgeport (owner since 1934); maintained by the Black Rock Community Council

events.note: First octagonal wooden tower, forty feet tall (LighthouseFriends)
Archive's 'Year Established' is 1809. The record and Rowlett give 1808.
Hurricane of 3 September 1821 laid the wooden tower flat; LighthouseFriends says every vessel in the harbour went ashore
Stone tower built to replace the wooden one; cost $2,300 (LighthouseFriends). The archive gives 1817 for the present tower.
Lamps upgraded to eight lamps with parabolic reflectors
Fifth-order Fresnel lens (LighthouseFriends). The archive gives 1856 as the original lens year.
Lighthouse Board report: a set of improved fifth-order lamps furnished and fitted to the lens
Lighthouse Service asked for $22,900 for two acetylene lights out in the water to replace the shore light
Congress transferred the lighthouse reservation to the City of Bridgeport for use as a public park
Keeper's dwelling burned to the ground
Tower restored after a 1993 fundraising effort by David Grant Grimshaw and Patricia Roche
Hurricane Sandy damaged the main entrance door, the tower base and the windows; repairs and revetment finished in 2017
Repointing, repainting, door replacement and revetment completed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive's place record gives 1809 as the year the station was established. LighthouseFriends dates the first wooden tower to 1808. The record uses 1808, from Rowlett's directory. Lit date is not given in LighthouseFriends.
The archive gives 1817 for the present tower. LighthouseFriends says the stone tower was built after the 1821 hurricane and cost $2,300 in 1823. The stone tower is the one standing.
The archive gives 1932 and its roster ends John D. Davies in 1931. LighthouseFriends gives 3 March 1933 and says Davies was keeper until then. D'Entremont gives 1933.
LighthouseFriends says a fifth-order Fresnel was installed in 1854; the archive gives 1856 for the original lens.

notes_for_editor: Sources: LighthouseFriends (facts; the Kathleen Moore interview, the 1821 storm passage and the 1931 request are its own quotations, read in the page text; their original sources are not checked); the USLHS place record (roster matched by name and position, 0.39 km); the Bridgeport Evening Farmer of 12 December 1910, p. 1 (OCR; the sea-wall sentence is contiguous and reads as a reprint of a federal harbor summary, so the story says so); the Light-House Board annual report for 1899, scan p. 106 (checked by corpus page: item 306, Black Rock, Connecticut; the printed page was not read); the Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1934 PDF p. 15 (checked: the 'Special legislation' list, enacted at the 73rd Congress, 2nd session). Wikipedia was read for leads only: it names the 1807 seller as Daniel Fayerweather and the builder as Abisha Woodward; LighthouseFriends and the archive say David Fayerweather and Elisha Woodward, and the story follows them. Not used: the 1894 Lighthouse Board paragraph about 'Black Rock' in the corpus, which concerns the Bridgeport Harbor light. LighthouseFriends says Kathleen Moore kept the light 62 years and gives roster-era service of 1871 to 1878; the story gives the archive span only, and the 21 lives are reported as LighthouseFriends' claim, unnamed and undated. The record's coordinates (41.14238, -73.217385, OSM) and the archive's (41 08.33 N, 73 13.04 W, about 0.4 km apart) were not reconciled. The record's characteristic F W and range 11 nm come from Wikidata and Rowlett and are not in the sources read, so they are not in the story. The focal height 12.2 m was removed: no source gives a focal height; the 12.2 m figure is the first tower's height. Judson Curtis and Elisha Woodward are listed by the archive as contractors with no dates; no source ties them to a specific tower. The 1808 and 1809 dates and the 1817 and 1823 tower dates are stated in the text as the sources differ. A Connecticut newspaper search (106 hits, 1808 to 1935, mostly the Bridgeport Evening Farmer 1909 to 1922, on harbor works and the Fayerweather purchase) was run; only the 1910 page above was read.
